title: Interface Change Conduit and LTS Guardrails
creator: Anjali Rao
description:
Goal: Define and implement an "Interface Change Conduit" — a prescriptive pipeline for any runtime API/interface change that may be breaking or require deprecation, paired with explicit LTS guardrails and automated upgrade tooling. This ticket codifies the policy, rollout gates, telemetry thresholds, and the minimal implementation of the conduit (CI checks + release workflow + runtime headers + migration helpers).

Scope: semantic versioning rules for the serving runtime (API surface and wire contracts), deprecation velocity (how quickly we can remove deprecated behavior), LTS channel requirements, canary/rollout gate definitions, and the first-pass upgrade assistant CLI and client-compatibility CI job.

Policy highlights (executive summary):
- Semantic versioning: major.x.y => breaking change in public wire/API contract or behavioral changes observable by clients (bump MAJOR). Minor/patch for additive/non-breaking or bug fixes. All releases must include a "compatibility note" in release metadata.
- LTS channels: maintainers will publish two parallel channels: stable (weekly/biweekly) and LTS (quarterly, backported critical fixes only). Breaking changes are never applied to LTS; only patches and security fixes with clear upgrade notes.
- Deprecation windows: for hosted API endpoints and runtime protocol fields, minimal deprecation period is 90 days for stable channel and 180 days for LTS-aware deprecation notices. We must provide migration steps and a generated shim where feasible.
- Rollout gates (Interface Change Conduit): all changes that alter public contracts go through the Conduit: 1) RFC + compatibility checklist, 2) CI compatibility matrix run (client SDKs + common runtimes), 3) opt-in canary (0.5% -> 5% traffic over 72h with automated SLO checks), 4) ramp to 100% if no signals, else halt and rollback.
- Telemetry thresholds for canaries: error rate increase >50% relative to baseline OR P95 latency regression >20ms OR token cost regressions >10% will trigger automated rollback. Thresholds can be tuned per-change via the RFC.
- Upgrade tooling: implement an "rwc upgrade-check" command that validates clients against a remote compatibility manifest and produces a migration plan. Include a server-side compatibility shim generator that can serve legacy requests (best-effort) for up to one major cycle.
- Communication: API responses must include structured deprecation headers (e.g., "X-Runtime-Deprecation: v3.0;remove-after=2026-07-01;migration-doc=https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/runtime-deprecations"). Release notes must include machine-readable metadata and a compatibility score.

Accepted trade-offs and decisions:
- We will not block all breaking changes from landing in main; instead, the Conduit provides early detection and staged rollout. This balances velocity and customer protection.
- Maintaining shims indefinitely is operationally expensive; policy limits shim support to one MAJOR cycle by default. Exceptions require Engineering + Product signoff.

Implementation plan (milestones):
1) Specification and RFC (DONE) — details governance model and compatibility checks.
2) CI compatibility matrix job (in progress) — expand test matrix to include latest client SDKs and an automated compatibility report (target: 2026-03-12).
3) Release workflow hooks (canary routing + metrics watchdog) — implement pipeline in release-bot and routing service (target: 2026-04-01).
4) Upgrade assistant (v0) — CLI that fetches compatibility manifest and offers a migration diff (target: 2026-04-15).
5) Deprecation header support in runtime and automated release-note metadata (target: 2026-03-22).

Acceptance criteria:
- RFC approved by Eng Leads and Product.
- CI job runs on every PR that touches public API, failing if compatibility score < 0.8 without an explicit override.
- Canary rollout automation in release-bot that can route 0.5-5% traffic and automatically rollback based on telemetry.
- Upgrade assistant that produces a migration plan for at least 3 common client SDKs (JavaScript, Python, Go).
- Deprecation headers present in runtime responses and linked migration docs in releases.

Risks and mitigations:
- False positives from compatibility checker (mitigation: allow override with documented risk and require Slack thread + product signoff).
- Operational complexity for shims (mitigation: cap shim lifetime and require automation for shim generation).
- Customer surprise from non-obvious behavioral changes (mitigation: expand integration test coverage and increase deprecation visibility in Console).

Rollout and monitoring:
- Dashboards: release-canary, compatibility-score, customer-error-budget-impact.
- Alerts: automated rollback on threshold breach; paging for persistent regressions.

Next steps: finish CI job, wire release-bot hooks, submit PRs for deprecation header, and prototype the rwc upgrade-check CLI.
